items.title: Rohingya rights group 'president' charged over unregistered organisation
items.summary: The Registrar of Societies Malaysia (RoS) said Zafar Ahmad Abdul Ghani, who had identified himself as president of the Myanmar Ethnic Rohingya Human Rights Organisation Malaysia (Merhrom), was charged under Sections 42 and 48 of the Societies Act 1966. "Zafar pleaded not guilty to both charges and claimed trial. The RoS said the charges followed an investigation by its enforcement division into Merhrom's activities on social media, including Zafar's statements and publications.

items.title: #NSTViral: Police chase lorry driving against traffic in Pasir Gudang
items.summary: PASIR GUDANG: A police chase involving a lorry driven dangerously and against traffic here went viral on social media. Several police patrol cars were seen pursuing the lorry and attempting to stop it, but the driver initially managed to evade them. One video showed the chase stretching for several kilometres before police eventually stopped the lorry at a traffic-light junction.

items.title: RM1mil BSN prize helps retiree build new surau for children in Kedah
items.summary: Arbaai, a retired civil servant, is the winner of the Bank Simpanan Nasional (BSN) Premium Savings Certificate (SSP) Millionaire Draw for August 2026, taking home a RM1 million prize. "I started saving with SSP by chance after receiving the Excellent Service Award (APC) in 2006, when one of the prizes was BSN SSP. That blessing eventually came through BSN SSP.

items.title: 44 rescued after flash flood hits JB kindergarten
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Forty-four people, including 37 children and seven teachers, were evacuated after flash floods hit Tadika & Taska Umiku Sayang in Jalan Muhd Amin. The Fire and Rescue Department said 10 personnel from the Larkin Fire and Rescue Station arrived at 4.14pm, about 21 minutes after receiving a distress call, and launched a rescue operation using a volunteer boat. All 44 victims were safely evacuated to the Medan Selera Tepian surau.

items.title: Uncovering the true craft of translation
items.summary: EVERY year on September 30, the global literary community marks International Translation Day, celebrating the craft of translators who carry stories across borders and grant them second lives in new tongues. To many, translation appears straightforward: an author writes, a translator replaces the words, and a foreign work arrives neatly bound on our shelves. Malaysian readers can choose between two Malay translations: Putera Cilik, translated by Ezzah Mahmud (Peanutzin, 2015), and Putera Kecil, translated by Azzah Abdul Rahman (Biblio Press, 2021).

items.title: Johan Setia reports highest unhealthy API level at 166, twenty areas in total experiencing bad air
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — Twenty areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 4.30 pm today, with Johan Setia in Selangor registering the highest level at 166. According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, four other areas in Selangor also recorded unhealthy air quality: Shah Alam (164), Klang (158), Petaling Jaya (155) and Banting (143). Meanwhile, 45 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while only three were at a good level.

items.title: Myanmar cleaner jailed 16 years for stabbing 80-year-old fruit seller
items.summary: Judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin sentenced Shofi Husson Sofo Rahman, 29, a United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees card holder, after he pleaded guilty to causing the death of Ah Kau @ Yow Chow Chong, not amounting to murder. An argument then broke out between Ah Kau and Shofi. Shofi took a knife and stabbed Ah Kau in the neck and body before fleeing the house.

items.title: Ex-cop loses final appeal over RM16,000 bribe to close commercial crime case
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: A former police corporal lost his final appeal to set aside his conviction and three-year jail sentence for accepting a RM16,000 bribe to help close a commercial crime case. A three-member Court of Appeal bench led by Datuk Azman Abdullah unanimously dismissed Azrol Khalil's appeal and upheld the decisions of the lower courts. However, the court rejected Azrol's defence that he was merely collecting the money on behalf of SP11.

items.title: UiTM Holdings RM157mil losses a legacy issue, says Fathul Bari
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The RM157 million in accumulated losses by UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd are a legacy issue dating from 2017 to 2021, not new losses under the current management. Its chairman, Datuk Dr Fathul Bari Mat Jahya, said the new leadership was committed to resolving the issue and would use Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's criticism as a catalyst to accelerate the recovery process. If UiTM Holdings is strengthened, its value will return to UiTM.

items.title: Immigration Dept denies Myanmar teen was repatriated
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Immigration Department has denied claims that a female Myanmar teenager was repatriated to her home country yesterday, saying she remains detained at an Immigration Depot. Its director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said checks confirmed that the teenager was not involved in yesterday's repatriation programme aboard a Myanmar military vessel. He added that internal controls were also implemented under the Immigration Regulations (Administration and Management of Immigration Depots) 2003 and the Director-General of Immigration's Standing Orders on the Administration and Management of Immigration Depots, taking into account the principles of humane treatment.

items.title: Republicans pour money into dozens of US House races previously considered 'safe'
items.summary: REPUBLICANS are pouring money into more than three dozen US House races previously considered "safe" after internal polling showed they could be vulnerable in the Nov 3 election, according to three Republican operatives familiar with the party's thinking. Since Sept 1, major Republican groups and megadonors have begun spending in at least 39 congressional races where they haven't previously deployed money this cycle, a Reuters review of spending by some of the largest Republican political groups shows. Republican Representative Bryan Steil is one telling example.

items.title: Sarawak hydrogen market viability still unproven, says analyst
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Sept 30 — Putrajaya should think twice about extending incentives to Sarawak’s hydrogen sector when it has yet to prove that there are enough buyers willing to pay commercially viable prices, according to an analyst. He said the basic problem with hydrogen was not Sarawak’s ability to produce it, but whether anyone wanted to buy enough of it at a price that made the business sustainable. “You can build the plant and produce the hydrogen.

items.title: Rain improves air quality in Johor, but haze persists in Pasir Gudang
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Heavy rain brought relief from the haze in Johor, with air quality improving in several areas, although four monitoring stations remained in the unhealthy category. In southern Johor, however, haze persisted, with Pasir Gudang recording the highest API at 164, followed by Larkin (162), Kota Tinggi (155) and Pengerang (152). The 4pm readings showed a clear contrast between northern and central Johor, where rain brought improvements, and southern districts, where air quality remained unhealthy.

items.title: Man who attempted to abduct six-year-old linked to 'gila isim', says exco
items.summary: MELAKA: A man who attempted to abduct a six-year-old girl in Ayer Molek last night is believed to have been experiencing a condition referred to as 'gila isim'. Melaka Education, Higher Education and Religious Affairs Committee chairman Datuk Rahmad Mariman said the man, from Sungai Petai, Alor Gajah, was also believed to have behaved unusually, including snatching a road user's mobile phone on the pretext of wanting to contact police. Rahmad, who is also Ayer Molek assemblyman, said the man was linked to 'gila isim', which he said was associated with claims of deviant teachings.

items.title: Flying this weekend? Malaysia Airlines urges KLIA passengers to arrive early amid Sepang F1 traffic
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — Malaysia Airlines advises passengers travelling from KL International Airport (KLIA) on Oct 2-4, 2026 to allow additional travel time to the airport, due to expected traffic congestion during the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit. “Passengers are advised to arrive at KLIA at least three hours before the scheduled departure time for international flights and two hours before the scheduled departure time for domestic flights to ensure a smooth process. “Malaysia Airlines said the check-in counters close 60 minutes before the scheduled departure time for both domestic and international flights,” it said in a post on X.

items.title: Mara targets RM1bil sales by Bumiputera automotive entrepreneurs next year
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) is targeting RM1bil or more in sales by Bumiputera automotive entrepreneurs next year through efforts to expand their participation and ownership in the sector. Mara chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the target was based on the agency's current performance, with 534 automotive entrepreneurs recording sales of more than RM660 million this year. He said TVET was also among Mara's key focuses in ensuring a continuous supply of trained workers for the automotive sector.

items.title: Petronas' sustainable fuel Mercedes-AMG F1's edge over other teams – Wolff
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Petroliam Nasional Bhd's (Petronas) use of advanced sustainable fuel (ASF) in this season's Formula One is set to be Mercedes-AMG's competitive edge against other teams this year. Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One team principal and chief executive officer (CEO) Toto Wolff said sustainable fuel is the way forward for the team especially as energy transition is becoming more prominent globally. "Sustainable fuel is the way forward.

items.title: Immigration Dept denies social media claim that Myanmar teen was repatriated, says she remains in detention
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — The Immigration Department today denied claims that a Myanmar teenage girl was among those repatriated to Myanmar yesterday, saying she remains in custody at an immigration detention depot. Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said checks by the department found that the teenager was not involved in the September 29 repatriation programme, which saw Myanmar nationals transported home aboard Myanmar naval vessels. “Checks by the department confirmed that the individual remains detained at an Immigration depot and was not involved in the repatriation programme for Myanmar nationals via Myanmar military vessels yesterday,” he said in a statement.

items.title: [UPDATED] No decision on minimum wage yet, earliest announcement on Budget day
items.summary: Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, at today's cabinet meeting, had directed that several aspects be studied before any announcement is made. On Saturday, Anwar said the government was dissatisfied with the wage levels despite rising productivity and high profits by some companies. Anwar said the government had already taken steps to raise wages, including increasing public sector salaries, raising the private-sector minimum wage to RM1,700 and setting a RM3,100 minimum wage for government-linked investment companies (GLICs).

items.title: Court sets Oct 30 deadline for autopsy report in woman murder case
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: The magistrate's court here today gave the prosecution until Oct 30 to obtain the autopsy report of a woman allegedly murdered by her boyfriend in January. "However, the prosecution has since received the CCTV report," she said. Unemployed Lim Chee Seong, 44, is charged with murdering his girlfriend, salon worker Lim Bee Lan, 41, at a house in Jalan Damai 2, Taman Damai 11, between 10pm on Jan 26 and 11am the following day.

items.title: Malaysia, Singapore test seven SOPs for RTS Link cross-border emergencies
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Malaysia and Singapore have tested their joint response to cross-border incidents involving the Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link as both countries step up preparations for its Jan 1 operation. The RTS Link Malaysia-Singapore Cross-Border Joint Exercise – Table Top Exercise, held here yesterday, focused on strengthening coordination between agencies from both countries in managing incidents that could disrupt RTS Link operations. The exercise, organised by the National Security Council in collaboration with Singapore's Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA), also tested and validated seven jointly developed standard operating procedures (SOPs) for managing cross-border incidents.

items.title: Ukraine's war costs for 2026 hit US$155 billion, PM says
items.summary: KYIV: Ukraine's total war costs will reach US$155 billion this year, and Kyiv is working to close a US$27 billion funding gap to ensure it can conduct active combat operations at the start of 2027, Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi said on Wednesday. Koretskyi said the government planned to cover US$7 billion of the gap through strict public finance austerity, budget optimisation and cost reallocation, and was in talks with partners on how to cover the remaining US$20 billion. "The situation regarding public finances remains challenging," Koretskyi said.

items.title: Zoo Melaka welcomes male black panther cub
items.summary: MELAKA: Zoo Melaka is celebrating the arrival of a male black panther cub, which was born naturally on July 22. Zoo Melaka said the cub was in good health, growing stronger and becoming increasingly active under its mother's close care. The cub's arrival adds to Zoo Melaka's ongoing wildlife breeding efforts and gives visitors an opportunity to follow its growth under its mother's care.

items.title: Supermarket awning collapses during heavy rain, damages three motorcycles
items.summary: KEPALA BATAS: A supermarket lobby awning collapsed during strong winds and heavy rain, damaging three parked motorcycles. Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said the incident occurred at Sunshine Supermarket in Jalan Dagangan 2, Pusat Bandar Putra Bertam Perdana, at 1.37pm. He said initial information indicated that the lobby roof structure collapsed due to strong winds accompanied by heavy rain, hitting three motorcycles parked nearby.

items.title: Myanmar man gets 16 years’ prison for killing 80-year-old fruit seller in Taman OUG
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — A Myanmar man was sentenced to 16 years’ imprisonment by the High Court today after pleading guilty to causing the death of an elderly fruit seller at a house in Taman OUG, three years ago. Judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin handed down the sentence on Shofi Husson Fozo Rahman, 29, and ordered the accused to serve the prison term from the date of his arrest on Sept 26, 2023. “The accused behaved well while in prison.

items.title: [UPDATED] Fahmi: Indonesia yet to respond on offer of firefighting assets
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia is still waiting for Indonesia to respond to its offer of assets to help put out fires there, government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Fahmi said the matter was discussed in the cabinet meeting following Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's visit to Indonesia, where he met President Prabowo Subianto. "So we are still following official channels and direct discussions between the top leaders," he said at a post-Cabinet meeting press conference. When asked whether the cabinet had discussed the haze and arrangements if it worsened this weekend, Fahmi said it was not discussed.

items.title: Primary Six pupil suffers burns after setting off firecrackers, Muar cops probe social media influence
items.summary: The incident also triggered panic among parents and the school community. Muar police chief Assistant Commissioner Raiz Mukhliz Azman Aziz said the 12-year-old boy was injured in the incident, which occurred at about 11am. Raiz Mukhliz said initial investigations later led police to detain the pupil to assist in the probe.

items.title: Selangor mulls appeal after High Court finds authorities liable for 2021 Taman Sri Muda floods
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — The Selangor government is considering whether to appeal a High Court ruling that found the federal government and two state authorities liable for negligence over the devastating 2021 Taman Sri Muda floods. The High Court yesterday ruled in favour of 50 Taman Sri Muda residents who sued the government and several public authorities over losses they suffered during the catastrophic floods in December 2021. Judicial Commissioner Shoba Rajah Dorai Rajah found the federal government, the Selangor Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) and Shah Alam City Council (MBSA), among the defendants, liable for negligence and related failures that contributed to the residents’ losses.

items.title: DOE: Over 500 hotspots in Kalimantan and Sumatra behind haze in Malaysia
items.summary: Department of Environment (DOE) deputy director-general (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) reported 327 hotspots in Kalimantan and another 191 in Sumatra yesterday, while one hotspot was detected in Sarawak. “ASMC also reported moderate transboundary haze affecting several areas in Peninsular Malaysia, Singapore and northwestern Borneo,” she said in a statement today. Azuri Azizah said the DOE would continue monitoring Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, hotspots and transboundary haze developments, taking meteorological information into account when assessing the situation and coordinating haze management measures at district, state and national levels.

items.title: Bank Negara imposes penalties on three companies for non-compliance amounting to RM40,400
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bank Negara Malaysia imposed administrative monetary penalties (AMPs) of RM22,000 on Wawasan Ilham (M) Sdn Bhd (WISB) and RM6,900 on SMJ Teratai Sdn Bhd for failing to comply with customer due diligence (CDD) requirements. Bank Negara said it discovered the breach following an on-site supervisory examination of WISB. It said Bank Negara discovered the breaches following an on-site supervisory examination of Ruhanmas.

items.title: Cabinet prays for Dr Mahathir's health as he remains under observation at IJN
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The cabinet has prayed for the health of former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad, who is under observation at the National Heart Institute (IJN). Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the cabinet also recorded its condolences to Dr Mahathir and his family following the passing of his wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali. "First, the prime minister, the cabinet and the government record their condolences to Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad and family on the passing of Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali, may Allah bless her soul.

items.title: PH sees room for cooperation ahead of Melaka election
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: PH sees room for cooperation with any party or coalition, including BN, in the Melaka election. PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said he had met PKR leaders in Melaka yesterday and heard views from PH Melaka. He said a meeting with BN would be held soon to explore possible areas of cooperation.

items.title: Sergeant major in the dock for leaking info on police raids
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU: A policeman pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to four charges of accepting bribes amounting to RM2,400 four years ago. Roslee Mamat, 43, a sergeant major with the Narcotics Criminal Investigation Division at the Setiu Police headquarters, was charged with accepting bribes ranging from RM400 to RM1,000 from an individual as an inducement to provide advance information on police operations or raids, thereby enabling the individual to take precautionary measures or flee to avoid arrest. MACC deputy public prosecutor Nur Amalina Najwa Mohd Ali prosecuted, while Roslee was represented by lawyer Mohd Fakhrul Fikri Mokhtar.

items.title: [UPDATED] Nepal agrees to expedite status confirmation of 55 untraced Malaysians
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Nepal has agreed to help expedite the process of confirming the status of 55 Malaysians who remain untraced following the disaster in the country, said government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. Fahmi said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had spoken to his Nepali counterpart yesterday, Balendra Shah, during which the latter agreed to the request. "Nepal's prime minister has informed of his agreement to help speed up the process of confirming the status of the 55 Malaysians who remain untraced following the disaster in Nepal," he told reporters at a post-Cabinet meeting press conference here.

items.title: Grab's GX Bank calls for expansion of government-backed credit guarantees to digital lenders
items.summary: Its chief executive officer Kaushik Chowdhury said expanding guarantee schemes, including the proposed RM10 billion Bank Negara Malaysia-Credit Guarantee Corporation facility, to digital lenders would allow them to provide lower cost loans to MSMEs. Kaushik also called for greater integration between licensed digital banks and government digital infrastructure through direct, low-cost application programming interface connections. Streamlining digital verification would reduce onboarding requirements and operational costs while expanding access to financial services among rural communities, gig workers and underserved groups, the digital bank said.

items.title: [UPDATED] 3,542 Myanmar detainees to be repatriated in second phase
items.summary: Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the 1,476 detainees in the first group were identified by the Myanmar authorities . "For the second phase, 3,542 Myanmar detainees have been agreed with Myanmar to be sent home at the next stage," he said at a post-cabinet meeting press conference here. He said Wisma Putra would hold discussions with Myanmar soon so that more Myanmar detainees in Malaysia could be accepted back after the second batch was completed.

items.title: US Senate blocks measure demanding report on rights violations in West Bank
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US Senate Republicans on Tuesday blocked a bid to require President Donald Trump's administration to report to Congress on increasing violence in the occupied West Bank, including the deaths of American citizens. The procedural vote was the latest sign of friction between US Democrats and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government over Israel's treatment of Palestinians and of Republicans' continuing strong support for his coalition. Israel has occupied the West Bank since 1967.

items.title: ‘Dinner, but no deal yet’: Fahmi says nothing formal between Pakatan and Bersatu for now
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 30 — Pakatan Harapan has yet to begin formal discussions with Bersatu over possible cooperation for the Melaka state election, despite a closed-door meeting between representatives of both sides earlier this week. PH communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said any decision on political cooperation would have to be made by the coalition's presidential council, adding that he had not received any information on formal negotiations with Bersatu. His comments came after PH and Bersatu leaders attended a closed-door dinner in Melaka on Monday night, fuelling speculation that the two sides could be exploring an electoral arrangement ahead of the state election.

items.title: 10 former Negri Sembilan excos vacate offices, return official vehicles
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Ten former Negri Sembilan executive councillors whose appointments were revoked have stopped using their offices at Wisma Negeri and returned their official vehicles. Former state Industry, Technology, Innovation and Digital Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, speaking on behalf of the former executive councillors, confirmed that they had received instructions from the State Secretary's Office to return their official vehicles. "The former executive councillors no longer come to their offices at Wisma Negeri.

items.title: Fahmi: Govt expects F1, KL Marathon and Le Tour de Langkawi to go ahead despite haze
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 30 — The government expects the Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, Le Tour de Langkawi and Kuala Lumpur Standard Chartered Marathon to proceed this weekend despite haze affecting several parts of the country, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. “For now, the government expects the three major events — LTdL, F1 and the Standard Chartered Marathon — to continue,” he said during a press conference here. He said Malaysia had also offered assets to Indonesia to help the country tackle fires contributing to the regional haze.

items.title: Touch ‘n Go to add 10 Enhanced RFID lanes for Malaysia’s MLFF transition
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — Touch ‘n Go Sdn Bhd (Touch ‘n Go) is expanding its Enhanced Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) network with 10 additional lanes by the end of the year to support the country’s transition towards a Multi-Lane Fast Flow (MLFF) tolling ecosystem. Currently, two Enhanced RFID lanes are already operational, located at the Ampang-bound Dato Keramat toll plaza on AKLEH, and the Putrajaya-bound Putrajaya toll plaza on the MEX Highway. Woon said the RFID lanes feature an enhanced technology that utilises two RFID antennas paired with an Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) camera.

items.title: KTM Komuter, ETS services resume after Batang Benar-Labu power line repairs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — KTM Komuter Klang Valley and ETS services have resumed normal operations after repair works on the overhead power line between Batang Benar and Labu were completed at 1.41pm today, Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) said. In a statement, KTMB said KTM Komuter and ETS services on the Pulau Sebang-Batu Caves-Pulau Sebang route were operating as usual, although some ETS journeys could still face temporary delays as train movements and schedules are readjusted. Earlier today, Malay Mail reported that services were disrupted from 6.24am after a 25kV overhead power line between Batang Benar and Labu was severed.

items.title: Anwar: Malaysia needs young talent to navigate diverse challenges
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 30 — The country needs a younger generation with determination, understanding and knowledge to take on the important responsibilities of driving national development, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said young people with such talent and leadership qualities were essential in navigating the various challenges and complexities of the country’s governance. Also present were Deputy Prime Ministers Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, and Cabinet ministers.

items.title: In Johor Bahru, man’s reversing mishap sends car into two vehicles and an eatery
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 30 — A 69-year-old man accidentally crashed his Toyota Camry into two vehicles and an eatery after apparently pressing the accelerator by mistake while reversing in Taman Daya here yesterday. Johor Bahru South police chief Assistant Commissioner Azrul Hisham Mohd Shaffie said police were alerted to the incident after videos of it went viral on social media at about 2.20pm. The aftermath of an accident at an eatery in Taman Daya, Johor Bahru, after a Toyota Camry crashed into two vehicles before ploughing into the premises on September 29, 2026.

items.title: Kuala Pilah school death: Five students allege bullying by 16-year-old suspect
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 30 — Five students have come forward to police claiming they had been bullied by the first suspect detained over the death of a Form Two male student in Kuala Pilah last Friday. The media reported that police had detained another 16-year-old male student yesterday in the investigation into the death of a Form Two student in Kuala Pilah last Friday. On Sept 25, a Form Two student was injured in an incident at a school in Kuala Pilah.

items.title: Free Rapid KL shuttle buses to Sepang circuit to run every 10–15 minutes from Oct 2–4
items.summary: According to travel information released by Rapid KL, passengers can board the direct service at KLIA 2, Bandar Baru Enstek and Mitsui Outlet Park. At KLIA 2, passengers can board at the Level 1 bus hub at Bays B1, B2 and B3. From KLIA 2, passengers can board the free Rapid KL shuttle to the Sepang International Circuit.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng calls for MACC action on Zahid over RM2.1b ministry overspending, cites UiTM precedent
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — Bagan MP Lim Guan Eng has urged the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) to initiate an investigation into Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi over an alleged RM2.1 billion budget overrun at the Ministry of Rural and Regional Development (KKDW). Citing official Finance Ministry figures, Lim noted that KKDW spent RM1.8 billion in 2023 against an approved budget of RM1.1 billion. In 2024, the ministry expended RM2 billion against a RM1.3 billion allocation, followed by RM2.3 billion spent against an approved RM1.6 billion in 2025.

items.title: No deal with Pakatan: Azmin says Bersatu preparing to contest Melaka polls alone
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia has ruled out working with Pakatan Harapan (PH) or any other political party in the Melaka state election, with secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali saying the party is preparing to contest on its own. Azmin also said Bersatu intended to contest under its own logo, as it did in the Negeri Sembilan state election, Berita Harian reported today. Among those present were Bersatu information chief Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz, Melaka Bersatu election director Datuk Seri Mohamad Ali Mohamad, Bersatu associate wing chief Datuk Seri R Sanjeevan and Melaka Bersatu information chief Datuk Seri Hishamiddin Abdul Karim.

items.title: Honda Civic driver gets attempted murder charge for ramming policeman at Ipoh roadblock
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 30 — A car wash worker pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to a charge of attempting to murder a traffic policeman on Sept 24. K. Viknes, 29, entered the plea after the charge was read out before Judge Norhayati Mohamad Yunus. According to the charge sheet, Viknes, who was driving a Honda Civic, attempted to murder Lance Corporal Badrul Izwany Pauzi, 29, by ramming the vehicle into the victim, knowing that the act could result in death.

items.title: Tanjung Rambutan care centre resident charged with murdering fellow patient
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 30 — A man was charged in the Magistrates’ Court here today with murdering a resident of a care centre in Tanjung Rambutan, near here, on Sept 3. The court, however, recorded no plea from Soo Kim Keong, 51, who is also a resident of the care centre, after the charge was read out before Magistrate Norizan Riduan, as murder cases fall under the jurisdiction of the High Court. Kim Keong is accused of murdering Chong Mun Long, 28, at the Grace Home Care Centre, Jalan Chemor, Tanjung Rambutan, between 3 am and 4 am on the said day.

items.title: ‘We are always open’: BN still negotiating political cooperation, says Asyraf Wajdi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said talks over Barisan Nasional’s (BN) approach to the Melaka state election are still ongoing, with its political cooperation arrangements yet to be finalised. According to Utusan Malaysia , Asyraf said discussions remained at the leadership level and noted that the Election Commission had yet to announce the election date. Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh had said on Sunday that BN would begin talks with other political groupings ahead of the 16th Melaka state election.

items.title: College student fails to strike out murder charge over Jalan Ampang collision that killed couple
items.summary: High Court Judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin made the ruling after allowing the prosecution’s preliminary objection to the application filed by Danish Raman Kamar Kumaresan on August 5. “After examining the submissions of both parties, the court allows the prosecution’s preliminary objection. Accordingly, the accused’s application to strike out the murder charge is dismissed,” said the judge.

items.title: Bidor petrol station shooting: Man hospitalised with bullet wound to shoulder
items.summary: TAPAH, Sept 30 — A 41-year-old man was reportedly shot in the left shoulder after two gunmen opened fire on his four-wheel-drive vehicle at a petrol station in Bidor Sentral yesterday. According to Berita Harian , Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the incident occurred at about 6.08pm after the victim drove his white Toyota Land Cruiser into the station to refuel. Police forensic investigators reportedly recovered one 9mm Luger bullet, four spent cartridge cases of the same calibre and bullet fragments at the scene, while further fragments and bullet marks were found on the victim’s vehicle.

items.title: Sarawak Flying Doctor Service helicopter crash: Police find no indication of foul play
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 30 — Police have found no indication of foul play in their investigation into the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash at Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, which claimed five lives, with the probe now nearing completion. Bukit Aman Management director and Sarawak Police Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah said police had taken statements from several witnesses, including those connected to locations visited by the crew members and the helicopter before the incident. As far as the police investigation is concerned, we have nearly completed our investigation,” he said.

items.title: Man jailed two weeks for trespassing at house linked to Sarawak deputy premier’s wife
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 30 — A 21-year-old man was sentenced to two weeks’ jail and fined RM1,500 in default one month’s imprisonment by the Magistrates’ Court here today for trespassing at a house under the control of Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Awang Tengah Ali Hasan’s wife. The offence was committed at 9.50am on September 24 at a single-storey house in Taman Sri Sena under the control of Datuk Dayang Morliah Datuk Awang Daud. According to the facts of the case, a complainant, who is Dayang Morliah’s brother, noticed the accused entering the house without any permission.

items.title: Babies born in Malaysia in 2026 expected to live 75.5 years, DOSM says
items.summary: “Three states exceeded the national level life expectancy (75.5 years) for 2026, namely Selangor (78.2 years), W.P. DOSM said life expectancy at birth in 2019 rose 0.4 years compared with 2016, with male life expectancy increasing from 72.1 to 72.5 years and female life expectancy also up by 0.4 years. Meanwhile, DOSM said life expectancy at birth in 2019 rose 0.4 years compared with 2016, with male life expectancy up from 72.1 to 72.5 years and female life expectancy also rising 0.4 years.

items.title: Johor court fines 15 men, including Chinese nationals, over fake job scam aimed at US citizens
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 30 — Fifteen members of a job scam syndicate targeting US citizens were fined between RM3,500 and RM4,200 each by the Magistrate’s Court here today after pleading guilty to conspiring to commit fraud through non-existent job offers. Before Magistrate Nurzihan Abdul Rehman, nine local men were fined RM3,500 each after pleading guilty when the charges were read out to them collectively. They were Liew Ming Hui, 23; Chong Yong Xuan, 25; Gan Kai Lin, 20; Gan Wei Xiang, 23; Myles Tan Yi, 21; Eldrick Tan Chin Lim, 24; Tan Hong Wei, 23; Dennis Chong Wen Wei, 28; and Chuah Kian Wei, 21.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan PKR urges swift end to state administrative impasse
items.summary: Its chairman, Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun, said the developments involved not only constitutional and royal institutional issues but also raised concerns over the continuity of the state administration, economic stability and public welfare. The former menteri besar said uncertainty over the status of members of the State Executive Council (Exco) could delay important matters requiring consideration and approval by the state authorities. The affected exco members are Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli, Datuk Zaifulbahri Idris, Datuk Mustapha Nagoor, Siow Kong Choon, Siti Nur Umaira Hasim, Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Suhaimizan Bizar, Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa and Datuk Razali Abu Samah.

items.title: MMEA ends One Fathom Bank search after recovering last body in Perak
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 30 — The body of the remaining angler reported missing at One Fathom Bank near Pulau Ketam on Sept 14 was found in waters off Kuala Kurau, Perak, yesterday. Selangor MMEA director Maritime Captain Abdul Muhaimin Muhammad Salleh said the body of Raja Mohd Rozi Raja Mohamud, 49, was found floating by local fishermen about 4.5 nautical miles southwest of the Kuala Kurau estuary at 5.25 pm. He said the fishermen alerted the Kuala Kurau Maritime Zone after spotting the body, which was wearing a blue shirt and camouflage trousers.

items.title: Sarawak police to enlist Interpol over Kuching convenience store attacks
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 30 — Police will seek assistance from international law enforcement agencies, including Interpol, to track several individuals believed to have fled the country in connection with attacks on convenience stores in several parts of Sarawak recently. Sarawak Police Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah, who is also the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) Management Department director, said three individuals had been arrested so far, while about 10 others had been identified as being linked to the group. Mohamad Zainal said police had also identified the misuse of business licences by some convenience stores involved in selling the top-ups and would write to the local authorities (PBT) for further action.
